01.r: Marks 'your silver' as the object of 'give'.
01.n: This small word marks a definite direct object and has no English equivalent; it is counted with 'Your silver'.

02.r: Silver used as money, the thing lent.
02.n: Gesenius gives the first sense as silver, so called from its pale colour. The Hebrew puts it first for emphasis: 'your silver you shall not give'. Of these translations only the BSB keeps 'silver'.

04.r: To hand over the silver as a loan.
04.n: The ordinary verb 'give'. The brief's lexicon includes 'lend' among its uses, and here it means to give on loan. The BSB says 'lend'.

05.r: The poor brother of the verses before.

06.r: In return for interest: as a loan that earns a charge.
06.n: The Hebrew 'for' (בְּ) marks what the silver is given in exchange for. Gesenius and BDB both give interest, usury; our English keeps 'interest' for this word in every verse (see Exodus 22:25 on this page).

07.r: In return for an increase on the food lent.
07.n: Gesenius gives this word's senses as multitude, then progeny, the increase of a family, and then interest, as if the increase of the principal, citing this verse and comparing Greek τόκος, from τίκτω, to give birth. A related word from the same root, תַּרְבִּית, appears in Leviticus 25:36 on this page; both are rendered 'increase'. Like 'your silver' in the first clause, it stands first in its clause for emphasis.

09.r: To hand over food on terms that bring a return.
09.n: The same verb 'give' as before. The KJV and Geneva say 'lend'; the BSB says 'sell', reading it as food sold for profit; the Douay-Rheims follows the Latin Vulgate, 'exact of him any increase of fruits'.

10.r: Food lent to the poor brother, to be repaid with more.
10.n: Gesenius gives first an eating, then food, especially corn, grain, provision.

_extra.11: αὐτῷ (to him): the Greek repeats 'to him' in the second clause, where the Hebrew does not.

01.n: The Greek article τὸ stands where the Hebrew has its object marker.

04.n: Dictionary form supplied; the brief gives none. δώσεις, 'you shall give'.

06.n: τόκος, interest, here in the dative: 'for interest'.

07.n: πλεονασμός, an increase, a surplus: 'and an increase', as the object of the second 'you shall not give'.

09.n: Dictionary form supplied; the brief gives none.

10.n: βρῶμα, food; the Greek makes it plural, 'your foods'.
